Seega Rules

A quick reference for how PaperGames plays Seega, the Egyptian game of placing and trapping.

The basic idea

The board
The board has 5x5 squares. Each side has 12 stones: Black (filled discs) and White (rings).
Placing phase
The game starts with an empty board. White begins: the sides take turns, each turn placing two stones on any empty squares except the centre, which stays empty. Nothing is captured while placing. When all 24 stones are on the board, the moving phase begins by itself.
Moving phase
Whoever began placing also moves first, and that first move has to bring a stone onto the empty centre. On your turn, move one of your stones one square across or up/down (never diagonally) to an empty square.
Capturing
If your move leaves an enemy stone between the moved stone and another of your stones, in a straight line across or up/down, that stone is captured and removed. One move can capture several stones in different directions. A stone that moves between two enemy stones itself is not captured. The centre is not a safe square.
Moving again
After a capture you may move again if that move captures too. PaperGames rule: the next move must be made with the same stone - just like a multi-jump in other games. You may also stop instead.

How a game ends

Passing
If you cannot move on your turn, you pass.
Winning
You win by capturing all of your opponent's stones.
Ending a blocked game
PaperGames rule, not a traditional one: after 40 turns in a row without a capture (20 for each side; a pass counts as a turn), or when neither side can move, the game ends. Whoever has more stones wins; equal numbers make a draw.
Resignation
A player can resign at any time, ending the game immediately in the opponent's favour.

Which version is played here

Seega has been played on 5x5, 7x7 and 9x9 boards, and the old descriptions differ in several details, for example what happens to a player who cannot move. PaperGames plays the 5x5 game with the rules above. The centre is not a safe square here, because none of the sources checked mentions one. Two points are PaperGames rules and are marked as such: moving again only with the same stone, and the end of a blocked game.

Sources

These rules follow: Wikipedia, "Seega (game)": https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seega_(game) · Ludii Portal, "Seega": https://ludii.games/details.php?keyword=Seega. The Ludii Portal refers to Lane (1836), pp. 356-357, Davies (1925) and Bolton (1890).
